The replay may show observable behavior, but opacity can limit what can be established about the path or its possible alternatives. The plan's reachable-and-stable condition should not be used to quietly declare such uncertainty resolved. If the uncertainty prevents a firm client-level conclusion, the case should not be forced into a definite classification on the strength of repetition alone.
Does 'classify only stable reachable divergences' imply that all other cases receive the same label?

No. It sets a restriction on what qualifies for classification under this replay plan. An unstable observation, an upstream difference not shown to be client-reachable, and an opaque execution can leave different questions open. The plan does not prescribe a single label for all of them.
I want the tests to be replayable witnesses where they support an incompatibility, not just inputs selected by an analyzer.

The synthesized input is only the starting point. The witness would need the client-level replay and its interpretable comparison between dependency versions. Five replays per version, pinned containers, and normalized outputs are intended to make that comparison inspectable; the plan does not assert that every synthesized input will yield a witness.
Has this plan established any recall or precision result?

No. It specifies how to synthesize inputs, replay each version five times in pinned containers, normalize outputs, and restrict classification to stable, reachable divergences. It reports neither a recall nor a precision measurement, and it does not state the outcome of any replay.
I'm executing the UpgradeWitness tests under both dependency lockfiles in pinned containers, five times for each lockfile. I'm recording normalized client outputs and flaky-run flags.

That puts the replay plan into operation. Each UpgradeWitness test is run against the dependency state identified by each lockfile, with five runs per state. The recorded normalized client outputs provide the observations for comparison, while flaky-run flags keep run-to-run instability visible. This activity does not yet state what the comparisons show.
Can you make the run count unambiguous?
It is five executions under the old dependency lockfile and five under the new dependency lockfile for each test—not five executions shared between the two lockfiles.
Why is it important to record the outputs from the client rather than just note whether the dependency changed?

The question is whether the upgrade affects behavior through the client. Recording client outputs lets the replay comparison address that question. A change within the dependency, without a client-level observation, would not by itself be a replayable witness of a client incompatibility.
What does running under both lockfiles contribute to a witness?

The lockfiles identify the two dependency states being compared. Running the same UpgradeWitness test under both makes its client-level observations relevant to that version comparison. The lockfiles alone are not the witness; the replayed test and recorded behavior are also needed.

They support a more consistent setting for the replays, so differences between recorded outputs are easier to interpret in relation to the two dependency lockfiles. Pinning is not, on its own, a guarantee that executions will be deterministic or that a particular difference is dependency-caused.

Is an unknown-target label the same as a positive incompatibility verdict?

No. It marks an unresolved possibility, not an observed behavioral incompatibility. A positive verdict needs client-level evidence appropriate to its claim; the label explains a limit on what the analysis can conclude about an unexercised path.

What does the recall part ask?

How is precision different?

Precision asks what share of positive incompatibility reports are correct. Recall asks what share of labeled incompatibilities are found. Neither can be inferred merely from the number of observed callback targets or from the fact that the regression includes 100 cases.
Does a 100-case regression mean 100 positive reports?

No. It specifies the number of cases in the regression, not the number labeled incompatible or the number of positive reports. Those are the relevant denominators for recall and precision, respectively, and they are not supplied by this activity.

If a witness replays successfully, does that make every uncertainty label on its verdict unnecessary?

Where do callback traces fit if the report already has a verdict?

Could the trace be read as a complete list of callbacks the client might reach?

And a trace might exist even when part of the analysis remains uncertain?

Not automatically. The replay can demonstrate a difference along the path it exercised, while reflection might still leave other targets or paths unresolved. The uncertainty should remain where it limits a broader inference; it need not negate the demonstrated observation.
